scenes.title: 1966 Sunlit Palo Alto Front Lawn: Tiny 3-Inch 'Safe Driver' Window Sticker vs Giant 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' Billboard (16.7% -> 76.0%!)
scenes.era: 1966, Tree-lined suburban street, Palo Alto, California

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1966 California mid-century suburban front porch and manicured green lawn: in the window corner gleams a **tiny 3×3-inch 'Be a Safe Driver' square sticker** (from Week 1), while on the front grass two weeks later stands a **massive, clunky, hand-lettered white wooden 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' billboard** blocking the porch view alongside a crisp **16.7% Cold Ask vs 76.0% After 3-Inch Sticker** placard!

positions.who: Jonathan Freedman / Volunteer #2 mannequin (in 1966 collegiate button-down shirt, chinos, and clipboard)
positions.where: standing on the sunlit front walkway holding up the photograph of the giant 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' lawn billboard while pointing from the tiny 3-inch window sticker to the 76.0% bar!

positions.who: Palo Alto Homeowner mannequin (in 1966 cardigan sweater at open front door)
positions.where: glancing affectionately at their own tiny 3-inch 'Be a Safe Driver' sticker in the window — then nodding warmly ('Sure, put the big sign up!') at 76% compliance!

props.name: tiny 3×3-inch 'Be a Safe Driver' window sticker vs giant clunky 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' lawn billboard
props.period_detail: hilarious visual scale jump from 9 square inches to a view-blocking yard monster

props.name: 4-Group Palo Alto Results Stand ('Cold Ask: 16.7% | Different-Topic Petition: 47.4% | 3-Inch Sticker First: 76.0%!')
props.period_detail: shows both the 4.5x sticker jump and 3x cross-topic identity proof

actions.verb_sequence: places the tiny 3-inch square sticker neatly inside the window corner in Week 1 -> two weeks later Volunteer #2 shows the giant 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' lawn-billboard photo -> Homeowner glances at their own sticker ('I'm an involved citizen!') and signs YES!

reactions.reaction: smiles proudly beside the enormous lawn sign while next-door Cold-Ask neighbors shake their heads 'No way!' (83% refusal)

scenes.wardrobe: 1966 California suburban style: crisp collegiate button-down and chinos; mid-century knit cardigan and slacks.
scenes.lighting: Bright high-key sunny California morning light.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ask cold to plant a monster 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' billboard in a manicured suburban yard and 83% slam the door — hand out a tiny 3-inch window sticker two weeks earlier and 76% say 'Dig right in!'

key_visual.description: a sunlit 1966 suburban front lawn and porch contrasting a tiny 3-inch window sticker with a giant 'DRIVE CAREFULLY' yard billboard and a 16.7%-to-76.0% compliance chart as a homeowner nods yes to a clipboard researcher

scenes.title: Study 1: A 2-Minute Soap Phone Quiz Opens Every Cupboard!

layout.description: Sunlit 1966 kitchen with rotary desk phone and open wooden pantry cupboards.

positions.where: answering 8 harmless soap questions by phone on Monday -> welcoming a 5-person product-counting crew on Thursday at 52.8% (more than double 22.2%)!

props.name: rotary kitchen phone & soap survey card ('22.2% -> 52.8%')
props.period_detail: proves even a 2-minute phone favor doubles intrusive 2-hour home access

actions.verb_sequence: answers quick phone soap check -> three days later opens pantry doors warmly

scenes.wardrobe: 1966 collared shirtdress and neat crew shirts.
scenes.recognition_hook: Eight harmless phone questions about dish soap on Monday more than doubled who let five strangers inventory their kitchen closets on Thursday!

scenes.title: Why Paying $5 for the Tiny Sticker Kills the Magic!

layout.description: Suburban walkway comparing an Unpaid 3-inch sticker (high 76% identity shift) against a Paid $5 voucher sticker (collapses back toward baseline!).

positions.where: showing that external payout gives an alibi ('did it for the voucher') that blocks the 'helpful citizen' identity shift

props.name: Unpaid Voluntary Vote vs Paid Voucher comparison card

actions.verb_sequence: declines the big billboard two weeks later ('I only put up the small sticker because you paid me!')

reactions.reaction: confirms voluntary unpaid micro-acts drive identity

scenes.recognition_hook: Pay people for the tiny 3-inch sticker and the 76% lawn-sign miracle collapses — only voluntary choices rewrite 'the kind of person I am'!

scenes.title: Hacking Your Own Habits With a '3-Inch Sticker' Week 1

layout.description: Warm morning room where running shoes sit beside a 'Week 1: Just Walk 3 Minutes' card leading smoothly to 'Week 3: 5K Run'.

positions.where: completing a tiny effortless 3-minute walk that casts an 'I show up daily' identity vote

actions.verb_sequence: laces shoes for tiny 3-minute step -> two weeks later strides smoothly out for full run

scenes.recognition_hook: Don't start Monday with a giant ugly billboard — start with a 3-inch habit sticker that lets your brain see itself as 'someone who shows up'!
